# The Absolute Suffers from Remoteness and Abstractness[^1]

But from the human point of view, no one can pretend that the absolutistic brand doesn't suffer from the faults of remoteness and abstractness. It is eminently a product of the rationalistic temper. It disdains empiricism's needs. It substitutes a pallid outline for the real world's richness. It is dapper; it is noble in the bad sense, in the sense in which to be noble is to be inapt for humble service.

[^1]: [[@Pragmatism - William James]]
